issue: C1's entire rationale for adopting Pipecat is turn-taking quality: 'turn-taking = Silero VAD (local, <1ms/30ms chunk) + Smart Turn v3... this is the FREE piece that makes it a conversation, not walkie-talkie'. But Smart Turn v3's Japanese-language end-of-turn support is never confirmed anywhere in the spec or in the cited research evidence. evidence/pipecat-decision-2026-07-04.md explicitly confirms Kokoro is 'Japanese-confirmed' (line 11) but makes NO equivalent claim for Smart Turn v3 -- it is only described as 'local, $0' / 'bundled ONNX'. This product is JP-cost-driven (the entire Reality Check / Goal 2 / C2 sections exist because of a JP user base and JP Google-cost problem), and C1 supports call_language in {ja, en}. If Smart Turn v3's turn-detection model is English-only or degrades on Japanese speech patterns/prosody, the JP call path reverts to exactly the 'walkie-talkie' failure mode the pivot exists to solve -- for the higher-priority language of the two.

fix: Add an explicit line to C1 (or a new OQ, resolved in-spec per the project's own no-open-questions rule) stating Smart Turn v3's actual JA support status, with a citation (github.com/pipecat-ai/smart-turn model card / training-language docs).
